author: Claude (cloud session), per PROJECT_OWNER/GPT decision under changeset AI_EXECUTION_BOUNDARY_V1_20260907
purpose: Turn the project's BOUNDED CHANGESET / ANTI-RECURSIVE-AUDIT prompt-level rule (AI_START_HERE.md) into a machine-checkable contract: a fixed structured-output schema plus default numeric/path budgets that governance_guard.py can validate mechanically, instead of relying only on an AI reading and following prose instructions.
scope_of_this_contract: This file defines defaults and schemas only. It does not itself declare or enforce scope for any specific changeset. Each changeset supplies its own scope_declaration (see scope_declaration_template) consistent with these defaults, or with explicit PROJECT_OWNER-approved overrides recorded in that changeset's own CHANGE_ROLES file.

document_semantics.note: A file or directory's RETIRED/ARCHIVED status only changes whether it is read by default in a normal session boot. It never implies deletion and never changes on-disk content.

default_budgets.note: These are the project's DEFAULT ceilings for a typical bounded changeset (e.g. AI_EXECUTION_BOUNDARY_V1_20260907 itself). A changeset that genuinely needs more -- for example NEXT_DATASET_COLLECTOR_IMPLEMENTATION, which will create many source/test files -- must supply its own scope_declaration with explicit, PROJECT_OWNER-approved budget_overrides. governance_guard.py always checks against the effective budget (override value if present, else this default), never silently loosens a limit on its own.

forbidden_paths: <repo-relative path prefix that must never be touched by this changeset>

budget_overrides.MAX_NEW_FILES: <int, optional -- omit to use default_budgets value>

enforcement_mechanism: governance_guard.py (repo root) implements two read-only, no-network, no-repo-mutation checks: (1) validate_output(candidate, schema) -- rejects any structured-output object with keys outside structured_output_schema.properties, missing required keys, or enum/type violations; (2) check_change_budget(scope_declaration, change_summary, defaults) -- checks a *declared* summary of a changeset's new files/dirs, scan/test/reconciliation run counts, and MASTER/CHANGELOG append sizes against the effective budgets (override if given, else default_budgets), and checks every new path against allowed_paths/forbidden_paths prefixes. It does not itself walk the git repository or infer newness -- the caller supplies the change_summary explicitly, keeping the guard a simple, auditable mechanical check rather than an autonomous scanner.
non_goals: This contract does not replace PROJECT_OWNER/GPT review -- it only prevents a subset of scope-creep and malformed-output failure modes mechanically, before a human ever has to notice them.

It does not attempt to detect every possible governance violation; it enforces the specific, previously-recurring failure modes this project has actually hit (unbounded MASTER growth, undeclared new files/dirs, unschema'd status output, silent scope expansion).
